5 observed episode-mean flows lie outside the strictly congested FD domain (0 < D/P < C). Their algebraic queue-speed values are retained and flagged. Equations and interpretation

Observed traffic

D=∑iqiΔt
Δt=112 h
x=DC
Tf=Lvf
P=t3−t0
wpeak=Lmin(vi)−Tf
w¯=∑iqi(Lvi−Tf)∑iqi
v¯=DL∑iHi

Flow qi is in vehicles/h/lane. D is in vehicles/lane; x and all times in the equations are hours. Hi is five-minute vehicle-hours per lane: bin count multiplied by the whole-link travel time L/vi. Recorded point speeds are whole-link speed proxies. Delay is not clipped at zero.

QVDF predictions

P^=max(fdxn,x)
wpeak^=TffpP^s
w¯^=θwpeak^
vt2^=LTf+wpeak^
v¯^=LTf+w¯^
α=θfpfds
β=ns
w¯^=Tfαxβ

A hat denotes a fitted quantity. The final reduced delay equation applies on the power branch. The calibration coefficients are shown in the optional QVDF-coefficients column group.

Triangular FD and queue state

kc=Cvf
ω=Ckj−kc
μ=DP
μ^=DP^
kq=kj−μω
vq=μkq

ω is the positive magnitude of the backward wave; its signed propagation speed is −ω. Use fitted μ for the fitted queue state. Jam density kj = 220 veh/mi/lane is an assumed closure constant. Neither queue-state speed is an independently measured target.

Capacity, S3 and comparison limits

C is the accepted detector S3 capacity, or the preserved profile 99.5th-percentile fallback. PeMS network metadata capacity divided by its lane count is a separate comparator.

S3 kc and vc describe the empirical S3 fit and differ from the triangular critical density. Pre-S3 capacity is a profile estimate, not network metadata.

APE=100|ym−yO||yO|

Here ym is fitted and yO is observed. A zero reference denominator is undefined (—). The separate CBI recovery-window flow is not the episode mean flow used in the queue-state calculation; its QC flag is included only for provenance.

Parameter fits are by corridor, direction and period, with the saved corridor-wide fallback when period support is insufficient. Fit-source counts refer to the calibration cohort, not just these 137 retained emission cases. Profile dates identify average profiles; Arizona dates label months. These comparisons use fitted sample results, not an out-of-sample validation set.
